messages:
sam: FYI hit flaky 429 behavior in prod integration — async python client just retries on Retry-After but ignores X-RateLimit-Reset, causing double waits and weird pacing.
elaine: can you paste headers you saw?
sam: sure — snippet from the proxy logs: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1770055000
Retry-After: 1
Content-Type: application/json
```
sam: current client path: uses Retry-After if present, otherwise exponential backoff. That means when Reset is further in the future we still do tiny retries and flood quota when it opens.
mike: hmm ok. We should prefer a normalized header parse: prefer X-RateLimit-Reset (absolute ts) -> compute delta, fallback to Retry-After (seconds), and last-resort backoff. Also unify for sync + async.
elaine: agree. Also the async typings are messy in the client helpers so people avoid using AsyncThrottle. I've got a typing + contextmanager idea: AsyncRateLimiter as async context manager with typed params.
tina: would we expose this as a public util or keep internal and wire it into Client.request?
sam: I think both: small public util in devex.utils.rate_limit with stable API and client uses it under the hood. That avoids copy-paste in service code.
mike: API sketch: ```python
class ParsedRateHeaders(TypedDict):
    remaining: Optional[int]
    reset_ts: Optional[int]  # epoch seconds
    retry_after: Optional[float]  # seconds

def parse_rate_headers(headers: Mapping[str,str]) -> ParsedRateHeaders: ...
```
Then AsyncRateLimiter.listen(response_headers) -> optional sleep seconds or raises RetryAfter.
elaine: for async: something like: ```python
async with AsyncRateLimiter.from_headers(headers):
    # will await if needed before issuing next attempt
    await client._send(...)
```
But maybe simpler: AsyncRateLimiter.wait_if_needed(headers) -> await.
sam: +1 to simpler wait_if_needed. Keep context manager for long-lived tokens.
tina: tests? integration harness should simulate different combos: only Retry-After, only X-RateLimit-Reset (in future), both present with conflicting shorter Retry-After.
mike: we also need to document precedence rules and add a small note in SDK upgrade guide.
elaine: I'll draft a tiny RFC + PR. Plan: add parse_rate_headers util, AsyncRateLimiter.wait_if_needed(headers, now_fn=...), a sync wrapper, unit tests for edge cases, docs.
sam: small implementation detail: Reset is epoch seconds server-side — need to allow both epoch and HTTP-date. Add parsing attempt for both formats.
mike: good call. Also jitter + cap when no headers present.
elaine: assigning to me. Will open PR with draft code and tests against the integration mirror. ETA EOD tomorrow.
sam: thanks! if anyone wants to help with tests ping me.
devex-bot: CI: PR 4321 — branch "devex/rl-headers-parse" created (checks queued) :robot_face:
elaine: will add type stubs so mypy is happy.
tina: thanks, this should reduce our false positives in Canary. :thumbsup:
sam: also consider exposing a small helper for user apps: ``retry_on_429(client, func, max_retries=3)`` — optional.
mike: maybe leave that for a follow-up. Keep first PR focused.
elaine: yep. I'll link the PR here when ready.
sam: ack :thumbsup:
